sections.content:
6,870 people

were counted on the census as "market research interviewers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Market research interviewers conduct interviews to collect information on the opinions and preferences of consumers, businesses, the electorate and other selected groups.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "market research interviewers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "market research interviewers", 12.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "market research interviewers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "market research interviewers" included:

  • leisure and travel service occupations (other)
  • horticultural trades
  • telephonists

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "market research interviewers" there were more women than men (59.6% compared with 40.4%).

This means "market research interviewers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "customer service occupations".

Men made up 40.4% and women made up 59.6% of "market research interviewers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "market research interviewers" included:

  • optometrists
  • authors, writers and translators
  • financial and accounting technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "market research interviewers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "market research interviewers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "market research interviewers", 14.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (61% compared with 39%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (80.4%) than self-employed (19.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
